headline: Plasmid-host links and phage variation relate to mobile gene content in gut bacteria
label: Microbial Mobilome And Genome Typing
summary: Gut phage catalogues from 1,069 samples and 105-strain metabolic models now link mobile elements to host and diet.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how mobile genetic elements and their host associations structure gut bacterial genomes. The ETEC preprint examines how plasmid-host associations shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli colonization factors. The TwinsUK phageome study builds a 116,740-vOTU catalogue from 1,069 gut metagenomes and links phage genomic variation to bacterial species and microbial metabolites. The C. difficile study addresses metabolic interactions rather than mobile elements directly: across genome-scale models of 105 strains under three diets with eight commensals, diet shaped interactions more than strain differences did. Together, the items point to host and environmental context as key determinants of gut genome content, though only the ETEC and phage work address mobile elements explicitly.
